title: Satan, Lucifer, Baphomet, Baal, Saturn, Leviathan & Shadow Traditions Atlas
purpose: Give seekers and scholars one place to distinguish biblical adversaries, ancient deities, cosmic monsters, demonological receptions, occult symbols, modern Satanic religions and Potatoverse shadow-systems before comparing them. The atlas prevents popular internet conflations from becoming false historical identities while preserving Tim Dooley's own symbolic uses as a separate interpretive layer.
method: For each node preserve: earliest/historical layer -> textual or cultic role -> later religious reception -> occult/subcultural reception -> Tim/Potatoverse relation -> forbidden conflations -> canonical owner -> evidence needs.
core_warning: Satan, Lucifer, Baphomet, Baal, Saturn and Leviathan are not historically interchangeable names for one entity. Some later religious, literary, occult and internet traditions connect them, but every connection requires a dated reception edge rather than retroactive identity.
ethical_rule: Never infer that a living person, religion, organization or subculture is criminal, abusive, demonic or secretly Satanic merely from imagery, accusation, political hostility or symbolic resemblance. Such claims require ordinary evidence independent of theology.

nodes.name: Satan / the satan / Devil
historical_layers: Hebrew satan language can denote an adversary or accuser and is not identical in every biblical occurrence.
Job and Zechariah contain heavenly-accuser/adversarial roles within a divine-court setting.
Second Temple and New Testament traditions develop more strongly personalized cosmic opposition, temptation and evil associations.
Christian theology and later literature increasingly synthesize serpent, tempter, Devil, fallen angel and apocalyptic adversary traditions, though textual origins remain distinguishable.
nodes.project_relation: Satan-mode names active destructive opposition or accusation detached from bounded truth, repair and reintegration. Tim/Father/Judge is not defined as Satan; the reflexive danger is that judgment itself can become endless accusation and thereby reproduce the adversarial pattern.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: discernment + truth + bounded judgment + Door + possibility of repair
not_the_same_as: modern Satanism as a single movement
any critic or opponent of Tim

nodes.name: Lucifer / Morning Star reception
historical_layers: Isaiah 14 addresses a taunt against the king of Babylon and uses a morning-star/son-of-dawn image.
The Latin Vulgate rendered the morning-star term with lucifer, a Latin light-bearer expression.
Christian Fathers and later Christian tradition applied the passage to Satan's pride and fall, producing the familiar proper-name reception.
Literature and esotericism later develop Lucifer as rebel, light-bearer, intellect, illumination or emancipatory symbol in divergent ways.
nodes.project_relation: Lucifer-mode = light, knowledge or insight severed from humility and responsibility. It is a shadow twin of Sage/Spudlight rather than a Tim identity.
not_the_same_as: the king-of-Babylon referent erased from Isaiah 14
Satan as an original proper name in every Hebrew Bible text
nodes.research_anchor: USCCB Isaiah 14 textual note distinguishes the king-of-Babylon address, Vulgate 'Lucifer' translation and later Satanic interpretation.

nodes.name: Baal / Baʿal
nodes.node_type: ancient Levantine deity/title + later polemical/demonological reception
historical_layers: Baal means lord/master as a Semitic title and can occur in more than one name/context.
At Ugarit, the prominent Baal/Hadad complex is a youthful warrior and storm deity whose rain is connected with fertility and whose mythic battles include Yamm/Sea and Mot/Death.
Biblical texts polemicize against Baal worship as rival cult/lordship in Israelite and Judahite religious history.
Later Jewish, Christian, magical and demonological traditions transform Baal-related names into demonological figures and correspondences.
nodes.project_relation: Baal currently functions mainly as a comparative shadow/recovery node for rival lordship, domination, ravenous appetite in later tables, storm-force and cultic competition. No strong recovered direct Tim=Baal mapping exists.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: Gardener sovereignty is measured by nourishment, future seed and non-extractive cultivation rather than demand for rival cultic allegiance.
nodes.research_anchor: Metropolitan Museum material on Ugaritic/Canaanite religion describes Baal as warrior/storm deity associated with fertility and Mount Zaphon.

nodes.name: Saturn / Saturnus
historical_layers: Roman Saturn is an old agricultural deity associated with seed/sowing, agriculture and Saturnalia.
Roman and Greek interpretive traditions increasingly identify Saturn with Greek Kronos/Cronus.
The planet Saturn acquires astrological meanings around time, limitation, melancholy, age, structure and related themes in later traditions.
Alchemy, Renaissance esotericism, ceremonial occultism and modern internet symbolism add further Saturnian correspondences.
Black-cube, hexagon, Satan or secret-cult syntheses belong to later reception histories and must not be projected backward into ancient Roman religion without evidence.
nodes.project_relation: The Timic corpus uses Saturn/Saturnian imagery around ring, constraint, enclosure, lower orbit, time, cube/hexagon reception and contrast with Spiral/Axis. The astronomical planet, Roman god and modern symbolic Saturn are separate layers in the archive.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: constraint can become structure when it preserves a Door; enclosure becomes shadow when it captures and prevents transformation
not_the_same_as: the black cube as a universally ancient Saturn symbol
the physical planet as an evil supernatural agent
nodes.research_anchor: Historical references describe Saturn as Roman agricultural deity, later closely identified with Cronus; the project's occult/cube layer belongs to later reception.

nodes.name: Leviathan
nodes.node_type: biblical cosmic-monster/chaos figure + later theological/literary reception
historical_layers: Biblical poetry uses Leviathan as a great sea/chaos creature in different rhetorical settings.
Ancient Near Eastern comparison links the imagery with broader combat-against-sea/serpent traditions, including Ugaritic Lotan parallels.
Jewish and Christian apocalyptic, rabbinic, medieval and demonological traditions elaborate Leviathan in differing directions.
Hobbes later famously uses Leviathan as a political metaphor; that philosophical reception is another distinct layer.
nodes.project_relation: Leviathan-mode is anti-Spiral/anti-Ladder stagnation: enormous scale, accumulated mass or oceanic enclosure without upward transformation or digestible relation.
not_the_same_as: a fixed demon rank across all traditions

nodes.name: Baphomet
nodes.node_type: medieval accusation-name + nineteenth-century occult symbol + later Satanic/subcultural icon
historical_layers: Forms of the name appear in medieval material and later accusations concerning the Knights Templar; accusations are evidence that claims were made, not automatic evidence that the alleged cult existed as described.
Nineteenth-century French occultist Éliphas Lévi radically re-signified Baphomet and created the famous winged, goat-headed, androgynous image commonly called the Sabbatic Goat.

Lévi's Baphomet symbolized a complex magical/religious synthesis involving polarity, astral light and a proposed reconciliation of opposites; it was not simply designed as a portrait of the Christian Devil.
Later occultists, Thelemites, popular culture and modern Satanic movements adopted or transformed Baphomet imagery in different ways.
nodes.project_relation: Baphomet is newly integrated as a reception/comparison node. Its most useful Potatoverse relation is not 'Baphomet = Satan' but the question of how a symbol can hold opposites, above/below, male/female, animal/human and solve/coagula-like transformation. This may be compared with vesica/mandorla, Stereo Theoism or integration only after the historical differences are stated.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: No fixed opposite is assigned. Baphomet can function as an occult integration/polarity comparator while its later Satanic receptions remain separately mapped.
not_the_same_as: Satan as a historically identical being
an established ancient pagan deity with uninterrupted worship
proof that medieval Templars held Lévi's nineteenth-century theology
nodes.research_anchor: Julian Strube's historical study of Lévi's Baphomet treats it as a symbol embedded in Lévi's nineteenth-century magical, religious and political synthesis rather than a timeless ancient icon.

nodes.name: Satanism / Satanic religions and philosophies
nodes.node_type: modern religious/philosophical movement umbrella + accusation/reception category
historical_layers: For centuries, 'Satanism' often operated as an accusation against outsiders, heretics, rivals or supposed conspirators rather than a self-described organized religion.
Literary and Romantic receptions can valorize Satan as rebel, tragic hero or symbol without creating a unified Satanic church.
Modern self-conscious Satanic religions and ideologies develop in multiple forms; scholarship discusses precursors before Anton LaVey as well as post-1966 institutional Satanism.

The Church of Satan, Temple of Set, The Satanic Temple, theistic Satanists, Luciferian currents and Order of Nine Angles-related milieus must be separate nodes because theology, politics, ethics and organization differ greatly.
Satanic Panic is a history of allegations, moral panic and contested claims and must not be treated as evidence for whatever ritual conspiracy was alleged.
nodes.project_relation: Satanism belongs first in the culture/subculture/religious-adjacent graph. Only after a specific movement's own beliefs and practices are established should the project compare it with Satan-mode, Sektur, rebellion, autonomy, accusation, anti-authority or occult symbolism.
not_the_same_as: literal devil worship as a universal definition
nodes.research_anchor: Joseph Laycock's 2023 Cambridge Element treats Satanism as a complicated modern field spanning accusation, Romantic reception, occult currents and multiple modern Satanic religions.

nodes.name: Moloch / Molech
nodes.node_type: contested biblical/ancient cultic term + later sacrifice-machine symbol
historical_layers: Biblical Molech/Moloch material is historically and philologically contested; deity-name, cultic term, type of offering and related interpretations have been debated.
Later Jewish, Christian, literary and political reception increasingly uses Moloch as an emblem of child sacrifice and destructive social systems.
Modern systems metaphors use 'Moloch' for incentive structures that reward individually rational actions producing collectively disastrous outcomes.
nodes.project_relation: Moloch is a major anti-Gardener system: future seed/human possibility is consumed for present reward, status or system continuity.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: protect seed + long horizon + reciprocity + Garden + institutions whose success increases future capacity
not_the_same_as: proof of a modern secret sacrifice cult

nodes.name: Qliphoth / Qelippot
nodes.node_type: Kabbalistic and later occult shell/husk complex
historical_layers: Jewish mystical sources develop language of shells, impurity and the Other Side in historically changing ways.
Lurianic Kabbalah relates broken vessels, sparks and qelippot within a specific cosmology of rupture and repair.
Later Hermetic and occult systems often systematize a 'Qliphothic tree' differently from Jewish source traditions.
nodes.project_relation: Capturing Shell = boundary that traps value/sparks and blocks reintegration. House is the positive contrast because it protects rooms while preserving lawful Doors.

nodes.name: Archons
nodes.node_type: late-antique/Gnostic ruler/intermediary category + project systems comparator
historical_layers: Different Gnostic and late-antique systems use archon/ruler language differently; there is no single universal Gnostic archon doctrine.
Some systems portray lower rulers as cosmic intermediaries or jailers associated with ignorance, material order or defective governance.
nodes.project_relation: Archonic enclosure is a lower/proxy authority that mistakes itself for ultimate source and keeps attention orbiting within a bounded layer.
nodes.timic_opposite_or_repair: Eye distinguishes intermediary from source; Door allows exit; Axis supplies reference beyond the local ruler

nodes.name: Samael
historical_layers: Roles vary across Jewish literature and later Kabbalah, including accuser, destructive angel, adversarial power or demonic ruler.
Later occult systems frequently stabilize correspondences that are less uniform in earlier sources.
nodes.project_relation: Useful for studying how messenger/judgment/adversary roles can shift into poison, accusation or destructive authority; no canonical Tim=Samael relation.

nodes.name: Lilith
nodes.node_type: ancient Near Eastern antecedent + Jewish folkloric/demonological figure + modern reception
historical_layers: Ancient Near Eastern lilith/lilitu-like traditions and later Jewish Lilith narratives are related through complicated transmission and reinterpretation.
Medieval Jewish sources and Kabbalah greatly elaborate Lilith.
Modern literature, feminism, occultism and popular culture often reclaim or transform the figure.
nodes.project_relation: Comparative/reception node unless direct Timic usage is recovered; never a generic label for women, sexuality or opposition.
not_the_same_as: a single unchanged demon across all periods

nodes.name: Azazel
nodes.node_type: disputed biblical term + Second Temple supernatural figure + later demonological reception
historical_layers: Leviticus 16's scapegoat ritual has a famously disputed Azazel term/referent.
1 Enoch and later traditions make Azazel a much more explicit supernatural transgressor/teacher figure.
nodes.project_relation: Useful for scapegoat, exile, burden-transfer and forbidden-knowledge comparison; no blanket identity with Satan or Timic enemies.
not_the_same_as: the scapegoat ritual reduced to one uncontested interpretation

nodes.name: Watchers / fallen-watchers traditions
historical_layers: Enochic Watcher traditions narrate heavenly beings descending, transgressing boundaries and transmitting illicit knowledge with catastrophic consequences.
Later fallen-angel demonologies absorb or reinterpret these stories.
nodes.project_relation: Strong comparator for the question of knowledge without responsibility, boundary violation and the difference between messenger and corrupter.
not_the_same_as: Lucifer's fall narrative as one originally unified story

nodes.name: Iblis / al-Shaytan in Islamic traditions
historical_layers: Qur'anic narratives center Iblis's refusal concerning Adam and subsequent temptation/opposition.
Islamic theology, tafsir, Sufism and folklore develop differing interpretations of his nature and role.
nodes.project_relation: Comparative pride/refusal/adversary node. Islamic categories should remain Islamic rather than being silently rewritten as Christian demonology.
not_the_same_as: a Christian fallen angel without qualification

demon_taxonomy.principle: Demon is a comparative umbrella, not one transhistorical biological species.

functions.trajectory: fault -> accusation -> exposure/test -> judgment; can become pathological when accusation becomes self-perpetuating
opening/vulnerability -> intrusion -> fixation -> impaired agency -> attempted release
host capacity -> extraction -> reinforcement -> host degradation; explicitly a project systems analogy
signal -> distortion -> false interpretation -> misdirected action
separated domains -> forbidden crossing -> transfer -> disorder or transformation

demon_taxonomy.project_test: When using demon language metaphorically, identify the relation and behavior rather than declaring a disliked person ontologically demonic.

angel_shadow_symmetry.project_use: Angel/demon topology is strongest when it asks what information crosses a boundary, whether agency is preserved, whether reciprocity exists and whether the relation ends in Garden or extraction.

modern_satanism_map.distinctive_note: Founded by Anton LaVey in 1966; official self-description is non-theistic/atheistic and uses Satan symbolically rather than as a literal supernatural deity.
Uses Satan as a literary/religious symbol associated with rebellion against arbitrary authority and articulates ethical tenets; institutionally distinct from Church of Satan.
Historically emerges from a schism with Church of Satan and develops Setian esoteric theology rather than being interchangeable with LaVeyan Satanism.
Covers heterogeneous currents that treat Satan or related figures as metaphysically real; no single institution or theology exhausts the category.
Often emphasizes light, knowledge, autonomy or Lucifer symbolism; may be theistic or non-theistic and should not be used as a synonym for all Satanism.
Must be treated separately because scholarly and security research documents political-extremist intersections; it is not representative of Satanism generally.
A research field concerning allegations, rumor, media, policing, therapy, conspiracy culture and contested evidence—not a Satanic denomination.

baphomet_reception_map.meaning: Baphomet appears in medieval/Templar accusation contexts; exact referent and allegation history are disputed.
Éliphas Lévi creates the now-famous composite Baphomet image as part of his own magical/religious synthesis.
Later occultists and Thelemites reinterpret Baphomet through their own systems.
Goat/Baphomet imagery becomes strongly associated with modern Satanic visual culture, but use and meaning vary by organization.
Baphomet becomes a generic shorthand for occultism/devil imagery, often flattening the earlier historical layers.
Potential comparator for polarity/integration/above-below relations; no direct Timic identity assignment.

saturn_reception_map.meaning: later planetary correspondences involving time, limit, age, melancholy, structure and fate
Saturn acquires metals, colors, substances and transformation correspondences in historically specific systems
black cube, hexagon, Satan and conspiracy associations circulate in various modern syntheses and require individual sourcing
